Referral to FMU:

•Anti D > 4, Anti C >7.5, Any anti K.
•Significant history of HDFN requiring exchange Tx, unexplained severe jaundice, titer of > 32.
•Rising titer.
•USG suggestive of fetal anemia.
•Other than C, D, K (any titer).
•MCA PSV >1.5MOM | Signs of anemia.
•Need for IUT

Causes of Alloimmunization

should be ascertained

•Blood Tx.
•Inadequate Anti D/ omitted Anti D injections.
•IUT, exchange Tx, Severe jaundice requiring phototherapy.

MCA – PSV:

•Weekly by expert
-Sensitivity 99%.
-False positive 12%.
-Sensitivity after 36 weeks.
•> 1.5 MOM => referral to FMU for FBS – (loss rate = 1 – 3% FBS).

IUT:

•O negative D-ve, O+ve, C-ve, K-ve
•CMV negative.
•Citrate phosphate dextrose.
•< 5 days old.
•HCT = 0.70 – 0.85.
•Irradiated within 24 hours

Exchange Tx:

•HCT 0.5 – 0.6.
•Group specific.
•Ab negative, K-ve.
•CMV negative. < 5 days old.
•Irradiated.

Top – Up:

•35 days old.
•Non – irradiated.
•Irradiation only if IUT already given.

High Risk women for Tx:

•Weekly cross matching.
•Sample should not be >12hrs old.

Used - same group ABO.

Blood - same Rh D. During

For - CMV negative. pregnancy

Tx - Kel Negative.

⇨Life Threatening, Haemorrhage => Transfuse blood + 1g prednisolone + full resuscitation.

Anti D Prophylaxis:

•Rh D Negative women:
-Anti D Ab – NO prophylaxis
-Non-Anti D Ab – Give prophylaxis.

Intrapartum care:

•CEFM
•In stable Ab levels and normal fetal tests => routine obstetric care.
•High risk Ab but no fetal anemia => 37 – 38weeks.
•Earlier if IUT done delivery.

 

Deliver in unit where facilities of exchange Tx are available.

Neonatal Care:

•Regular Hb and Bilirubin monitoring.
•Regular neurological assessment – sensorineural hearing loss, kernicterus.
•Avoid dehydration.
•Need for phototherapy/ Exchange Tx.
•Neonatal Anemia:
-Early due to maternal Ab – hemolysis
-Late due to suppression of Erythropoiesis especially in IUT.

 

Top – up Tx (if symptomatic).

Role of erythropoietin.

No long-term consequences of Ab on women health but an antibody card should be carried in case of transfusion.
